faqs.q: When will the selected applicants be announced?
faqs.a: The result will be announced on 16th October 2026.

faqs.q: How Can I Apply for Fully Funded and Partially Funded Slots?
faqs.a: To apply for a fully or partially funded scholarship, please complete the general application form. All submissions are reviewed by our independent, international selection panel, which ensures a transparent process for final scholarship decisions.

faqs.q: Can I Attend the SDG Innovation Summit If Not Selected for the Scholarship?
faqs.a: If you aren’t selected for a scholarship, you can still join us at the summit by choosing either the Self-Funded Package or the Forum Access Package. Regardless of your funding status, you will enjoy the same full experience and privileges as all other participants.

To help with your visa application, the GYN will provide an official invitation letter, proof of accommodation, and the program location. While we are happy to offer guidance throughout the process, please note that the final decision rests with the embassy, and we cannot guarantee visa approval.

faqs.q: What should I do if I do not have a passport at the time of application?
faqs.a: You can still apply! Simply upload a copy or enter the number of your National Identity Card (NIC), or any student ID in place of the passport details for now.

faqs.q: How can I pay my application fee?
faqs.a: You can securely pay the application fee using a debit or credit card, Google Pay through a trusted Stripe payment gateway.

Application fees are standard for many international conferences and youth programs. The fee supports our application, review, and selection process and helps us manage applications from participants worldwide. It does not guarantee selection.

faqs.q: Am I required to provide proof of English language proficiency?
faqs.a: No, English test scores (such as IELTS or TOEFL) are not required for this application.

faqs.q: Need Assistance or Want to Contact Us?
faqs.a: You can reach us via email at contact@thegyn.org

faqs.q: How will I find out about my selection and results?
faqs.a: All applicants will receive an email with their results. We will also post the final list of selected delegates on the GYN Facebook and Instagram pages. Follow us on Facebook and Instagram

items.title: Passport Bingo
items.text: An icebreaking challenge that sent delegates around the venue to find peers matching five prompts — from multilingual speakers to fellow travelers and gender-equality advocates — building the summit's first connections and a social-media trail under #FMST26.

items.title: World Got a Problem — Phase A
items.text: Delegates chose the SDG they were most passionate about, formed teams, elected a group representative, and identified one significant global problem to solve — with guest speakers and fellows on hand as mentors. An evening sightseeing tour (6:30–9:00 PM) gave the group a chance to unwind and take in Bangkok beyond the summit halls.

items.title: World Got a Problem — Phase B: Present Your Solution
items.text: Each team took the stage for five to six minutes to present their proposed solution to a panel of judges, scored on innovation, relevance to their SDG, feasibility, sustainability, presentation and teamwork.

items.title: Certificates, "04:04" & Cultural Night
items.text: The summit closed with Certificates of Participation and a "04:04 — hear you out" reflection session, followed by the optional Cultural Night: a celebration of unity in diversity with traditional attire, an open dance floor, and a Rabindra Sangeet performance in Japanese, German and English by cultural director Dr. Dipa Das. The event ended with an official group photograph of the whole FMST 26' community.
